root_cause.text: A race condition in __ceph_setxattr where required_blob_size is computed before __build_xattrs() releases and reacquires the lock, allowing handle_cap_grant() to update the xattr tree (increasing its size), making the prealloc_blob size check stale and causing the subsequent BUG_ON in __ceph_build_xattrs_blob() due to insufficiently sized prealloc_blob.
root_cause.evidence: Commit message states "Commit d93231a6bc8a moved the required_blob_size computation to before the __build_xattrs() call, introducing a race." and "The prealloc_blob size check that follows still uses the stale required_blob_size computed before the rebuild, so it passes even when prealloc_blob is too small." Patch fixes by recomputing required_blob_size after __build_xattrs() returns.

bic_trace_step.reason: The code in commit 355da1eb7a1f introduces a race condition in ceph_setxattr() (lines ~713-728). After computing required_blob_size under spin_lock, the lock is dropped only if reallocation is needed, and after reacquisition it recalculates. However, after the final __set_xattr and spin_unlock, the prealloc_blob size is no longer guaranteed to match the xattr tree because another thread (e.g., handle_cap_grant) can concurrently add/modify xattrs via __build_xattrs before __ceph_build_xattrs_blob() is called. The BUG_ON in __ceph_build_xattrs_blob() (line ~483) assumes the prealloc_blob is sufficient, but no re-check or resizing is done when building, so a concurrent update can cause the BUG_ON to trigger. No fix is present in this version.
